items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: she had a young sister called Boggs who was very beautiful and we all had eyes for her. Sometimes we would go walking and take turns walking with Boggs

ctx.x: One day I was out walking with one of my distant cousins that lived downstairs who's name was June, and two other boys in the neighbourhood named George Burr and Theodore Means. A nice little woman who must have been about 28 years old stopped us and asked if we could sing. Then she told us that she was a social worker and organist at a Presbyterian church and she would like to form a quartet of 4 boys. She offered to give us piano lessons and teach us some religious songs. We accepted her offer and a few nights…

The only one of us that had a piano at home was June, so he and I could practice there, but we could get into the church any time we desired and George Burr, Theodore Means and myself did most of our practising there. The woman's name was Miss Hargrave and she lived in a very nice section of Walnut Hills. We used to go to her home some nights to play our lessons and learn songs. The main reason we liked to go to Miss Hargrave's house was because she had a young sister called Boggs who was very beautiful and we…
Now I think we all tried to get our piano lessons better than the next one just to show off in front of Boggs. We began to attend the church quite frequently and also sang at special church meetings.
